newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Property issues pull up Manila shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Property issues pull up Manila shares at close.

text.p: Philippine shares rose on Wednesday as renewed interest in property issues outweighed selling in several blue chips, traders said.

"The market's climb is led by the property sector. There's improved sentiment on Empire East Land Holdings Inc after their buyback and other property issues followed," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
The main index ended 25.10 points higher, or 0.90 percent, to 2,823.35 points.
The property sub-index posted the biggest gain among the six sub-indices, climbing 3.13 percent to 1,423.28 points.
Empire East Land Holdings was the most heavily traded issue of the day, closing 50 centavos higher at 3.70 pesos. The issue has risen 90 centavos, or 32 percent, in the last two sessions.
Empire disclosed in late trade that it had bought back 6.356 million shares at threee pesos apiece on Tuesday.
Index heavyweight and the country's biggest property firm Ayala Land was the fourth most actively traded share ending one peso higher at 22.50 pesos.
Traders said the market bought oversold property issues.

Some said an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission on possible price manipulation in Empire shares had cleared suspicions the stock had fallen last month because of financial troubles.
In the broader market, losers outnumbered gainers 57 to 54 but turnover rose to 2.3 billion pesos from the previous session's 1.75 billion.
Diversified Securities executive vice-president Jose Ricardo Garcia said he expected follow-through buying on Thursday.
Asiamerit's Lee said the market would continue its selective, sectoral stock picking.
